title: Vocab Match
intro: Match each word or phrasal verb to its meaning. Everyday phrasal verbs and useful adjectives, one pair at a time.

A2.why: You get up when you get out of bed. Waking up is opening your eyes.
Look for means try to find: the sheriff looked for the stolen horse.
Turn on starts a machine or a light. Turn off stops it.
Huge is much stronger than big: a huge ranch.
Tiny is much stronger than small: a tiny kitchen.
Cheap means low in price. It can also sound negative: cheap and nasty.
Begin and start mean the same: the film begins at eight.
Furious is much stronger than angry.
Put on is for clothes: the cowboy put on his hat.
Come back means return: we came back from Alicante on Sunday.
Tired means you need rest. Tiring describes the thing that makes you tired.
Delicious means very tasty: a delicious paella.

B1.why: Give up means stop trying, or stop a habit: he gave up smoking.
Find out means discover information: find out the train times.
Carry on means continue: carry on walking until the church.
Put off means postpone: the match was put off because of the rain.
Run out of means have none left: we've run out of milk.
Look after means take care of: she looks after her grandchildren.
Set off means begin a journey: the wagons set off at dawn.
Turn down means refuse: he turned down the job in Madrid.
Get on with someone means you like each other: I get on well with my neighbours.
Pick up means collect: I'll pick you up at the station.
Turn up means appear or arrive: a stranger turned up at the saloon.
Make up means invent: he made up an excuse.

B2.why: Come up with means think of: Jenner came up with the idea of vaccination.
Get away with means not be punished: the outlaws nearly got away with it.
Look up to means admire: she looks up to her mother.
Put up with means tolerate: I can't put up with the noise during Fallas.
Break down is for machines and cars: the car broke down near Requena.
Bring up means raise a child: she was brought up in Valencia.
Take over means gain control: the bank took over the company.
Fall through is for plans that don't happen: the sale fell through.
Make up for means compensate: a good dinner made up for the long wait.
Rule out means exclude: the doctor ruled out a broken bone.
Run into means meet by chance: I ran into an old friend at the market.
Look into means investigate: the marshal promised to look into the robbery.

C1.why: Dwindle means slowly become smaller: the gold dwindled and the miners left.
Meticulous means extremely careful about detail: a meticulous surgeon.
Ubiquitous means found everywhere: mobile phones are ubiquitous.
Candid means frank and honest: a candid interview.
Feasible means it can realistically be done: a feasible plan.
Scrutinise means examine very closely: scrutinise the contract.
Reluctant means unwilling: he was reluctant to see a doctor.
Pivotal means at the centre of things, critically important: a pivotal moment.
Elusive means hard to catch: the elusive outlaw was never found.
Resilient means you recover quickly: Valencia is a resilient city.
Obsolete means out of use: bloodletting became an obsolete treatment.
Lucid means clear: a lucid explanation.
